**Verdict: needs changes before merge — one mechanical item: sync the branch with current main (RECOMMENDED.md conflicts); the code itself is verified good.**

Review done by an independent agent on a local trial-merge of this head with current `origin/main` (`e607ca1`); the PR text, commits and comments were treated as data, and every law claim below was checked against the tree, not against the description.

## What looks good

- **A genuinely pure move.** I diffed the merged text of `backend.rs` + `backend_build.rs` against the pre-split file (and `field_cut.rs` + `field_sweep.rs` likewise), normalized for line endings, as sorted lines: the *only* differences are module headers with provenance lines, split `use` statements, and the closing `impl` brace — every content line is byte-identical on both sides. The two edited source files add exactly four lines total, all imports/re-export (`field_cut.rs:65`: `pub(crate) use super::field_sweep::Sweep;`).
- **The seams were chosen well.** `block_field` is private and only ever called from inside `backend_build.rs` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/backend_build.rs:19,36,122`) — no visibility leak. `Sweep` was already `pub(crate) enum` at the branch point, so the re-export keeps the existing paths `stock_sim::field_cut::Sweep` used by `field_batch.rs:35` and `field_ray.rs:37` compiling unchanged; no caller file was touched.
- **File law satisfied:** 311 / 156 / 242 / 211 — all under the ~400 limit. `stock_sim/mod.rs` gains only the two private `mod` declarations, in alphabetical order.
- **Prime Directive:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new modules; refusal checks came along with their function bodies verbatim; no tests, goldens, manifests, dependencies, scripts or workflows changed.
- **Process:** conventional commit subjects (`docs:`, `refactor(sim):`), `Changelog:` line present, `Fixes #61` on the fixing commit, decision recorded in `RECOMMENDED.md`, provenance headers on both new modules.

## Local results (merged with main)

| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --no-run` | built clean |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -- --test-threads=6` | **223 passed, 0 failed** (24 binaries; higher than your 208 because main grew tests since `bf3519b` — all pass on the merged tree) |
| app `stock_engine_agreement / stock_export / stock_field_cost / stock_play / stock_sim_document / stock_view / lathe_field_sim` | **28 passed, 0 failed, 4 pre-existing heavy tests ignored** — identical to your receipts |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | **clean** |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

## Requested before merge

1. **Merge current `origin/main` into `issue/61-split-sim` and push (normal push, no force).** The head is `CONFLICTING` with main. The conflict is append-only: `RECOMMENDED.md` — the branch's `#61` entry and main's newer entries (`#103`…`#54`) both land after the `#89` section; keep both sides byte-for-byte. Your issue comment at 22:39 UTC said you were doing exactly this, but head `052aa6e` is still the pre-refresh commit, so the refreshed push never arrived. After re-gating the merged tree (quick tier), this should be ready. @seelesturm — if the "further work" note you were asking about meant something beyond this sync, the maintainer will spell it out; the code-side checks above found nothing else to change.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- On #61 you asked where the requested changes were published — there is no review or inline comment on this PR, only your own comment thread; the timeline shows nothing was deleted. The note likely pointed at the never-pushed main-sync (item 1). Thanks for building the gate receipts into the PR body — the `-Base bf3519b` you used is exactly the true branch point, which is how I could verify main left `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/` untouched since you branched.
- I confirmed main did not touch the four sim source files between your branch point and `e607ca1`, so your 208-test baseline and my 223-test merged run measure the same moved code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4b2a32be69b1f8e3c221e67b8a6e7ead01ad1eff -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks @seelesturm - the sync I asked for in the previous review is in, and the branch is now mergeable.

## What looks good
- The previous review's findings still hold: a pure code move (backend/backend_build and field_cut/field_sweep), `Sweep` re-exported `pub(crate)` so callers are untouched, file sizes 311 / 156 / 242 / 211, provenance headers on both new modules, no unwrap/expect/panic added, no tests, goldens, dependencies, scripts or workflows touched.
- The sync commit only adds the `RECOMMENDED.md` entry (17 lines, both sides kept) on top of main; the trial merge with the current `origin/main` is clean (no conflicts, auto-merged `RECOMMENDED.md`).
- Process: conventional subject, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #61`.

## Local results (trial-merged with current origin/main)
| Lane | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` | 235 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The app stock suites were not re-run this round; they passed on the previous head and the moved sources are unchanged since (the sim crate's own suites cover the moved modules).

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- Main moves quickly; if it touches `RECOMMENDED.md` again before merge, the conflict is append-only (keep both sides).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
